summary: Regional failover causes model-pin to be lifted, canary instances evicted and traffic routed to fallback variant
description:
Issue summary:
During an automated regional failover (us-east -> us-west) for a dedicated customer we observed that their model version pin was unexpectedly lifted for a subset of routes. Canary instances for the pinned model were evicted and traffic was routed to the configured fallback variant (smaller quantized model), causing higher error rates and degraded quality for ~12% of requests.

Impact:
- Customer: TextFlow Inc. (dedicated)
- Duration: ~2026-03-10T19:05Z to ongoing (partial mitigation applied 2026-03-11T03:40Z)
- Affected traffic: ~12% of API calls for the customer across two services (content-generation and summarization)
- Symptoms: sudden quality regressions, increased application error reports, user-visible mis-summaries. No billing/credit impact reported yet.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-e1-textflow (reserved GPU cluster)
- Control plane region failing over: us-east-1 -> us-west-2
- Customer pin: tf-internal-llama-13b-v1.3 pinned at route level with canary group of 2 instances
- Fallback model: tf-internal-llama-7b-quant-v1

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Triggered automated regional failover due to networking incident in us-east (internal failover test and later observed in real incident).
2) Control plane moved scheduling decisions to us-west controllers; scheduler rebalanced pods.
3) During reschedule there was a short window where the route-level pin flag was missing from routing table for the customer's routes.
4) Canary instances for the pinned model were evicted (preempted or failed scheduling) and fallback routing activated for those sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Model pin should remain honored across control plane transitions; canary instances should be rescheduled without lifting pin for in-flight routes. Fallback should only activate when no compatible instance is available and should respect pin override until explicit policy change.

Actual behavior:
- Pin flag was not present in the reconciled routing snapshot sent to envoy/edge for ~5–15s for some routes during failover. Traffic was therefore evaluated against fallback routing policy and steered to the fallback model for affected requests.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Manually forced route pin through the console for the customer (route-level reapply) which restored correct routing for the majority of traffic by 2026-03-11T03:40Z.
- Increased canary replica floor for the customer's dedicated pool to reduce eviction risk during scheduler churn.

Investigation notes:
- Initial SRE logs show the control-plane reconciler completed a partial reconciliation and then restarted; the reconciliation step that re-attaches route pin metadata to the routing table may be non-transactional and could be replayed out-of-order.
- Eviction traces indicate preemption events on two canary GPUs due to binpacking decisions during failover. The scheduler did not prioritize pinned canary placement.
- Edge service (envoy) received a routing snapshot missing pin metadata (snapshot version drift observed) for a short window.
- Related to previous tickets SUP-4721 (canary fallback misroute) and SUP-8234 (stale route cache during gradual rollout).

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering (Serving Runtime + Scheduler) to add a transactional reconcile loop ensuring route pin metadata is applied before advertising new routing snapshot to edge (ENG-3810).
- Scheduler: add an eviction protection policy for pinned canary replicas during control-plane transitions (ENG-3822).
- Support: compile customer impact report and coordinate postmortem with TextFlow.
- Ops: add automated alert when route_snapshot_version_for_route != control_plane_version for >5s for any dedicated customer.

Resolution notes (partial):
- Route reapply by Support restored pinned routing for main routes; per-route canary replica floor increased. Full engineering fix scheduled.

References:
- Slack thread: #support (link: slack.com/archives/C04SUPPORT/p1700059000123456)
- Dashboard: serving-runtime/route-snapshots (internal dashboard link)

comments: Maya Patel (Support): Customer reported quality regression after automated failover; opening incident and applying route reapply as immediate mitigation.
Evan Brooks (SRE): Observed snapshot version drift; collecting reconciler logs and eviction traces. Assigned to Serving Runtime and Scheduler teams for follow-up.
Sofia Chen (Serving Runtime Eng): Hypothesis: reconcile writes metadata in two separate steps; will instrument and propose a transactional write. (ENG-3810)
Diego Ramos (Scheduler Eng): Scheduler weight logic didn't prioritize pinned canaries during binpack migration; proposing 'pin-protection' heuristic. (ENG-3822)
TextFlow Inc (Customer): Confirmed degraded output quality is resolved for major routes after manual reapply; requesting timeline for permanent fix.
resolution: Manual route reapply restored correct routing; increased canary replica floor to reduce future eviction risk. Engineering tickets ENG-3810 and ENG-3822 opened for permanent fixes. Postmortem scheduled with customer.
